reason: The approved GR13 scope and both complete page inventories were reviewed. Local proof and scope defects need the single repair round; no gap was found that cannot be resolved locally. No repair has yet been made, so consumer dispositions are pending the repair review.

findings.reason: Clause (b) includes coincident boundary points in its strict-convexity condition. Their constant geodesic does not have its interior in C, so the definition needs an explicit distinct-endpoint convention and degenerate-segment rule. This changes the public Definition and triggers consumer checks.

Steps 2.1–5.1 establish containment and uniqueness only for endpoints q,q' in C, but clause (c) invokes the Definition’s closure-endpoint condition. Extend the endpoint estimates and uniqueness argument to distinct q,q' in the closure, with the degenerate case governed by the corrected Definition.

The Statement requires a special exponential-coordinate ball with temporal u⁰, while consumers such as lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions (a), lem-gr-basic-limit-curve 5.1, and thm-gr-length-upper-semicontinuity L1 use the cone and length conclusions on arbitrary strictly convex normal balls. The cited normal-neighborhood result has broader scope; establish that scope or supply an exact argument supporting every consumer.

Step 5.1 asserts that a convex normal ball for gε contained in C can be used for the whole curve γ:[0,1]→C. It need not contain γ, and its gε exponential displacement is not the original g displacement D²p. Thus Fε≤0 on [0,1] does not follow. Replace this perturbation step with a complete causal-cone argument; also justify the timelike-curve passage in 4.1.

Step 5.1 takes sup‖Dv‖ over the closed product of coordinate balls, but clause (c) only ensures the corresponding open product lies in W. Shrink s so the closed product is contained in W before taking this supremum.

Fact L4 and step 3.1 need the joint inverse smooth at arbitrary pairs in a convex normal C, but lem-gr-joint-exponential-diffeomorphism (c) proves it only near the diagonal. Supply the local-diffeomorphism argument using normality at every base point and invertibility of each exp_q differential; the same gap is used in lem-gr-causal-curve-initial-cone-step 2.1, thm-gr-normal-neighborhood-causal-cone 4.1, and thm-gr-length-upper-semicontinuity L2/3.2.

Step 1.1 uses positive star-shapedness to justify exp_q(tw) for negative t; star-shapedness does not give −εw∈W_q (openness near 0 does). Step 3.1 also incorrectly infers that a curve returning to q is constant on [0,s]. Use a local temporal chart to rule out returns, and repair the non-diagonal inverse use in 2.1.

Step 2.1 says the set of parameters with σ(t)=p has measure zero because otherwise σ′=0 on a positive-measure set, but does not supply the absolutely-continuous level-set fact. Prove that fact locally or use the available local time-coordinate monotonicity; the inference is needed to apply reverse Cauchy–Schwarz almost everywhere.

Step 1.2 treats N as unit timelike, although the framework only gives a time-orientation field; normalize it to n. Step 3.1 circularly covers the entire γ arc by sets already contained in I⁺(p), which is what the proof is trying to establish, so its uniform δ conclusion is unsupported. Replace it with a finite local push-up construction.

Step 1.1 claims continuity supplies t₀ with the whole tail γ([t₀,1]) in a cone ball centered at γ(t₀). Continuity only gives a tail in a fixed neighborhood of γ(1); no such moving-center radius is established. Give a valid local openness argument.

Steps 3.1–3.2 assert without sufficient estimates that the interpolating geodesics converge uniformly and their speeds converge almost everywhere, including a uniform o(sᵢᴺ) displacement error. Step 4.1 also needs a finite common adapted-chart bound for the interpolants. Supply these arguments for the stated mesh-refining partitions.

Clause (i) promises uniform convergence on [0,b] although αₖ is defined only on [0,bₖ]; step 4.1 evaluates αₖ(t) for t>bₖ when bₖ<b. Specify a common-domain reparametrization or endpoint extension and prove the convergence and bounds for it.

Fact L2 says a limit of past-timelike vectors is past timelike because the cone is open, which is false; limits may be null. Step 5.1 relies on this for the infinite weighted sum. Use the fixed positive timelike summand plus the convergent sum of past-causal summands to prove the result.

Step 5.2 applies lem-gr-causal-curve-conventions (d), which covers future-inextendible curves on [0,∞), to a maximal flow line on (α,β) with finite β. Supply the finite-end one-sided extension needed to obtain an inextendible curve with the same future endpoint, or construct its past tail directly.

The remark says predictability readings of Cauchy levels, a global-simultaneity reading of the temporal function, and preferred-observer readings of flow lines are adopted in post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain. That postulate adopts the Lorentzian model and classical domain but does not make those additional assumptions. Recast them as optional interpretations requiring separate adoption.
